about: Tesla Roadster 2026 suspension rig for Unreal (generated by roadster_wheels.py).
frame: Blender metres: origin on the ground under the wheelbase midpoint, +X forward, +Y car's left, +Z up. Static ride height = wheel centre at the unloaded tyre radius.
to_unreal: position_cm = (x, -y, z) * 100; a rotation of angle a about Blender axis (ax, ay, az) is a rotation of -a about Unreal axis (ax, -ay, az); quaternion (w, x, y, z) -> (w, -x, y, -z).
mesh_convention: Every Susp_* mesh is modelled in its static pose with zero rotation and its origin at 'pivot'. To reproduce the static pose place the component at the pivot with no rotation.

joint_types.hinge: rotate about 'axis' (right-hand rule, Blender frame) through the pivot by the table angle (degrees, 0 = static).
joint_types.rigid: upright: place the origin at table.wheel_centre and apply table.upright_quat (rotation from the static pose, about the origin). Steering: additionally rotate about the current kingpin axis (LBJ->UBJ) through LBJ by steer_table.kingpin_deg.
joint_types.aim: keep the origin on 'pivot' (or on the moving point named in pivot_follows), and rotate so that static_dir maps onto the current direction pivot->target (minimal rotation, e.g. FQuat::FindBetweenNormals).
joint_types.aim_scale: as 'aim', then scale along local axis 'scale_axis' by table.spring_scale.
joint_types.spin: additionally spins about its own axis with the wheel (same angle as the wheel).

travel_definition: travel_m = vertical motion of the wheel centre from static (+ = bump). Tables are solved with the full linkage geometry (wishbones, upright, track rod/toe link, pushrod, rocker, damper).

parts.name: Susp_FL_Upright
parts.driven_by: wheel travel (+ steering on the front)

parts.name: Susp_FL_TieRod
parts.pivot_follows: steering rack: pivot.y += steer_table.rack_m * (+1 on both sides; rack moves as one piece)

parts.name: Susp_FL_Spring
parts.pivot_follows: damper body (moves with Susp_FL_Damper's rotation about its pivot)

steer_table.note: steer_deg = road-wheel yaw (+ = nose left, Blender +Z); rack_m = rack displacement along +Y (both track rods move together). Solved at static height. Unreal's physics steer is + = right, i.e. steer_deg = -degrees(W.Steer).
